title: Sequence affinity validator and canary workflow for KV profiles
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight validator and automated canarying workflow that verifies new per-model KV cache performance profiles against the live sequence distribution before wide publication. This ticket covers sequence-affinity fingerprinting, a deterministic compatibility check, automated canary rollout orchestration, and a failure detection + rollback policy for published profiles. The goal is to reduce regressions for long-context workloads when pinning model-version-specific KV retention and prefetch policies.
acceptance_criteria: Validator computes sequence-affinity fingerprints for incoming request streams and matches them to profile compatibility buckets
New profile publication triggers a canary rollout to 1% of traffic for 24 hours by default
Canary monitors key SLOs (p95 latency for tokens, token cost per 1k, tail loss rate) and raises an automated rollback if regressions exceed thresholds
Dashboard widget shows canary vs baseline deltas for each profile in Redwood Console
Playbook documented: how to override automated rollout, trigger manual diff checks, and force-pin a stable profile
tasks: Design sequence-affinity fingerprint schema and compatibility rules (data sketch that fits telemetry limits)
Implement validator service that can be run as pre-publish hook and as runtime checker during canary
Add canary orchestration in profile-publishing pipeline with traffic routing knobs and TTL
Wire metrics and alerts into Console: p95 latency, per-token cost, kv-hit-rate, generation error rates
Create PRD and automated integration test harness that replays traces against new profiles
Document rollout and rollback playbooks in Confluence
decisions: Use a compact locality-preserving hash over tokenized prefix statistics (n-gram density, avg seq len, attention sparsity signal) as the affinity fingerprint to keep storage cheap
Canary default: 1% traffic for 24 hours and automatic abort if p95 latency regressed by >10% or token cost increased by >15%
Validator will be implemented as a lightweight Go service colocated with the profile-publisher and exposed as an HTTP preflight endpoint
We will not ship deterministic cross-model mappings in this iteration; compatibility will be conservative and guided by fingerprint distance thresholds
tradeoffs: Compact fingerprints reduce telemetry and storage but increase false positives for edge sequence types
Conservative compatibility thresholds reduce risk of regressions but may delay publishing optimized profiles for niche workloads
Running runtime checks during canary adds some latency to the publishing path; mitigated by asynchronous background validation for non-blocking publishes
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev): unit tests and synthetic trace replays locally (target: Mar 1)
Phase 2 (staging): enable validator + canary orchestration on staging with curated long-context workloads (target: Mar 8)
Phase 3 (beta): opt-in beta for internal teams and three pilot customers, monitor for 2 weeks (target: Mar 15)
Phase 4 (GA): enabled in profile publisher; default canary active for all profile publishes (target: Mar 22)
Rollback: automated rollback will revert published profile and mark it as blocked; manual rollback steps documented in playbook
metrics: average token cost per 1k tokens served
tail loss rate: fraction of requests with >X token-generation retries
canary delta alerts count and false-positive rate of validator compatibility
